Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

Robinhood's Internal Audit team provides independent, objective, and timely assurance on the effectiveness of our governance, risk management, and internal controls — helping strengthen the frameworks that keep Robinhood and its regulated entities running with integrity. We partner closely with Robinhood Markets (RHM) leadership, the Company's Board of Directors, and its Committees to surface risk insights and drive meaningful improvements across the business.

RHM is the parent company of Robinhood's lines of business, including Brokerage, Crypto, and Cash services. We're looking for a Senior Manager, Crypto Operations to join the Internal Audit team and help us build a best-in-class audit practice for one of the most dynamic areas of our business.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA and New York, NY offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

Who we are:

About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team
Stripe offers an interesting middle ground between joining a small startup and going to work for a multinational company. We have systems and processes optimized for early-career professionals. You will be in an environment that prizes rigor, discipline, and reliability—from our products, from our ways of working, and from our colleagues. You will learn how the best teams put together extremely reliable systems, and you will be responsible for operating these systems, with adequate backup when things get tough.
The Security organization is dedicated to building and maintaining a secure financial infrastructure platform. By joining this team, you will be on the front lines, engineering solutions that protect the sensitive data and systems underpinning a huge portion of the world's economy. You will contribute to core security functions like threat detection and rapid incident response, building and scaling the platforms that manage vulnerabilities, and proactively performing offensive security assessments to identify weaknesses before they can be exploited. This is a chance to apply software engineering principles and new technologies such as AI to solve complex, high-stakes security challenges, ultimately ensuring that Stripe's mission to increase the GDP of the internet is achieved securely.

What you’ll do
As a Security Engineer New Grad you will have the opportunity to work across various security disciplines and own projects from start to finish. Your work will focus on securing Stripe's complex environment by applying software engineering principles to security challenges.
  • You will learn and apply the principles of secure-by-default design by working closely with product and infrastructure engineering teams.
  • You'll develop a foundational understanding of various security domains, such as threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, or offensive security.
  • You'll learn to act as a security subject matter expert, tailoring answers to both engineers and non-engineers.
  • You'll contribute to the development of internal tools and automation to scale security efforts across Stripe.
  • You will participate in threat modeling discussions, learning to balance security requirements with product advancement and user experience.
Responsibilities
  • Work on cross-functional projects, directly collaborating with other engineers
  • Give meaningful feedback on code reviews and technical designs
  • Contribute to our overall security posture by continuously improving security processes, tooling, and defenses.
  • Develop a deep understanding of Stripe’s security primitives, frameworks, and invariants.
  • Provide actionable insights to help identify, prevent, detect, and respond to anomalous or potentially malicious activity.
Who you are:
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements
  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s program in Computer Science or related field (graduating by Summer 2026)
  • Some experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Java, Ruby, Python, JavaScript, Scala, and Go. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present
  • Experience from either previous internships or working collaboratively on multi-person coding projects (in a university or professional setting)
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts
  • Aptitude to think like an attacker and reason through different approaches to reducing security risk.
Preferred qualifications
  • Experience in code review practices, and an understanding of how to safely update production systems
  • Familiarity with navigating and managing work in large code bases
  • Prior experience or course work in cyber security, digital forensics, or incident response (e.g., through log analysis or capture-the-flag events).
  • Familiarity with foundational security concepts such as the OWASP Top 10 web application vulnerabilities.
  • Basic knowledge of SQL or experience analyzing medium to large data sets.
  • Exposure to cloud computing platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • An adversarial mindset, understanding the goals, behaviors, and TTPs (tactics, techniques, and procedures) of threat actors.
descriptions.job-1ooj8az:
GoMining runs a portfolio, not a single product: Digital Miners, the GOMINING token, GoMining Card, Simple Earn, Wallet, Miner Wars, Academy, Travel, Launchpad and the VIP programme. Each of them ships, launches and promotes on its own rhythm — and today those messages reach the same user through the same channels without a single owner making sure they add up to one coherent story.

That owner is this role.

You'll sit at the centre of marketing as the connective layer between product go-to-market, brand, performance, content, CRM, community, design and PR. Half the job is orchestration: owning the communications calendar and running launches end to end, on time, across every channel. The other half is the message: making sure what we say about any product is clear, consistent, on-brand and worth a user's attention.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with company-wide visibility. You will not manage a team — you will manage the flow of work between several of them.

What you'll do

Orchestration — own how communication gets made and shipped

    • Own a single, company-wide marketing communications calendar: every product launch, feature release, campaign, promo and announcement in one place, with owners and dates.
    • Run launches end to end - both product and brand comms. Take the go-to-market input from product marketing leads and turn it into a channel plan — CRM (email, push, in-app inbox), in-product surfaces, community, social, website and blog, app stores, paid support assets, PR — then drive it to delivery.
    • Write the briefs. Translate business goals into creative and content briefs that designers, motion designers and copywriters can actually execute against, with clear deliverables and deadlines.
    • Be the single window into the design and production team. Prioritise, sequence and unblock requests instead of letting every stakeholder queue separately.
    • Hold the timeline. Chase dependencies across product, legal, compliance and finance so assets are approved and live on the date we committed to.
    • Coordinate joint communications with partners, collaborations and sponsorships.
    • Close the loop: pull post-campaign results with the analytics and CRM teams, run the retro, and turn what you learn into the next brief.

Message — own what we say and how it sounds

    • Build and maintain the messaging architecture across the portfolio: what each product promises, to whom, in what words, and how the products connect into one proposition.
    • Turn technical and financial mechanics — mining rewards, tokenomics, cashback, yields, VIP tiers — into copy a first-time user understands without a glossary.
    • Own tone of voice and message consistency in practice, not just in a deck: review outgoing communications against brand and messaging guidelines before they ship.
    • Maintain the shared toolkit — messaging docs, key-message one-pagers, FAQ and objection handling, launch templates — so other teams stop reinventing product copy.
    • Write and edit the high-stakes pieces yourself: launch announcements, product pages, campaign concepts, executive and partner-facing materials.
    • Work within the advertising and financial-promotion constraints of each channel and jurisdiction, together with legal and compliance, so approved copy is also compliant copy.
    • Track how competitors and the wider crypto and fintech market communicate, and bring back what's worth noting.


What success looks like

First 1 month — the calendar exists and is trusted; every product's messaging is documented in one place; the brief-to-delivery process is running without you being chased.

First 3 months — launches ship on schedule with a full channel set as the default, not the exception; message consistency across channels is visibly better; each launch produces a documented result and a next-step recommendation.

  • 4+ years in marketing communications, product marketing, integrated campaigns or brand communications — in-house at a fintech, marketplace, consumer app or scale-up, or agency-side with comparable clients.
  • Proven end-to-end ownership of multi-channel launches: you can walk us through campaigns you ran from brief to results, and say honestly what worked and what didn't.
  • Strong writing and editing in English (C1+). You'll be assessed on real copy, not on adjectives in a CV.
  • Genuine project management ability — prioritisation, dependency tracking, working to deadlines and budget across teams you don't manage.
  • The ability to hold a high creative bar while saying no, moving a date, or telling a senior stakeholder their request is out of scope.
  • Comfort with complex products: you enjoy the work of understanding a mechanic properly before writing about it.
  • Data literacy — you read campaign performance and use it to change the next brief.
  • Experience coordinating external agencies or creative studios.

Would be a plus

  • Experience in crypto, Web3, mining, trading, neobanking, payments or investment products.
  • Familiarity with advertising restrictions on financial and crypto products across ad platforms and jurisdictions.
  • Experience building brand or messaging systems from scratch rather than inheriting a finished one.
  • Additional languages.
  • Professional growth: support for courses, conferences, and English learning (up to 100% coverage).
  • Work-life fit: remote or hybrid format with flexible hours across international teams.

  • Recognition programs: structured performance reviews and team awards.

Partnerships and Business Development Manager

Location: New York City, 3-4 days per week in the office. Travel is mainly to conferences.

About Fence

Fence is building the modern infrastructure for asset-backed finance.

Today, asset-backed finance is still administered through spreadsheets, PDFs, manual reconciliation, slow drawdowns, bespoke legal and capital-markets processes, and fragmented information between originators, lenders, investors, SPVs, agents, and servicers. This is not just inefficient back office work. It is one of the reasons capital moves slowly, assets are hard to finance, and private credit markets remain less liquid, less transparent, and less programmable than they should be.

Fence replaces the spreadsheets, PDFs, and email with modern infrastructure based on APIs,AI, smart contracts and stablecoins.

In the near term, this makes Fence the tech-native facility agent for modern asset-backed finance: the operating layer that runs the facility and the SPV end to end. The larger vision is to enable the instant originate-to-distribute model for every asset originator: assets born with the data, controls, eligibility checks, cash-flow logic, and investor visibility required to be financed and distributed continuously.

Joining Fence means helping build the operating system for how capital moves into assets and back again.

The Mission

Your mission will be to make sure every lender and originator in US asset-backed finance knows Fence, and that the right ones are talking to us.

This is not a generic SDR role. It is a business development role for someone who can open doors with lenders, private credit firms and fintech originators, walk them through the product, understand their pain points, turn those conversations into real opportunities, and continue to build Fence's presence in the market.

What You Will Own

  • Pipeline generation: Build a steady flow of qualified leads, that convert to real opportunities from every channel: self-sourced outbound, referrals, inbound, events and marketing campaigns.

  • New conversations: Open relationships with ABF lenders, banks, private credit firms, asset managers and fintech originators, and run intro calls, demos, recurring touch points and follow ups required to identify opportunities.

  • Qualification and handoff: Identify where Fence can act as the facility agent, map the counterparties, pain points and timeline, and hand opportunities to our Capital Markets team ready to move forward.

  • Market presence: Own Fence's conference calendar and represent us at industry events. Plan and host Fence events, from private dinners to larger gatherings, with our Marketing team.

  • Pipeline discipline: Keep an honest, up-to-date pipeline where every lead has a clear next step and nothing goes cold.

  • Market feedback: Bring what you hear in the field back to Growth, Marketing and Product to sharpen who we target, how we explain Fence, and what we build next.

Who You Are

You are a relationship builder with real sales and finance fluency. You know how lenders and originators think, you enjoy being in the market, and you can hold your own in a capital-markets conversation.

Strong candidates will likely have:

  • 4 to 7 years in fintech sales or business development, capital markets, structured finance, or private credit.

  • Working knowledge of asset-backed finance: how facilities work and who the players are.

  • An existing network across lenders, private credit firms, or fintech originators.

  • A track record of building pipeline from scratch through outbound.

  • Experience representing a company at conferences or organizing industry events.

  • Spanish is a plus.

Why You May Not Be A Fit

You may not be a fit if:

  • You mostly worked inbound leads or managed existing accounts, and have not built pipeline yourself.

  • You have only sold SaaS without institutional-finance fluency and would struggle to hold a conversation with a structure finance professional.

  • You need a mature playbook, collateral and a defined territory to get started.

  • You prefer to stay behind a screen rather than meet people in person and at events.

Location

New York is the default location for this role, hybrid.

Why This Role Matters

Fence is moving from founder-led commercial conversations toward a repeatable institutional GTM motion.

The top of the funnel is where that starts. If we get this role right, Fence reaches every relevant lender and originator in the US, the Capital Markets team spends its time closing real opportunities, and the market starts to see Fence as the default way to run asset-backed finance.

Compensation

$140,000 - 180,000 annual base salary, plus equity and performance bonus. Variable compensation is uncapped, with accelerators.
